newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Inflation hastens fall of Zimbabwe stocks.
newsitem.headline: Inflation hastens fall of Zimbabwe stocks.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index dropped 0.8 percent or 81.32 points on Wednesday, dealt a fresh blow by a sharp rise in annual inflation to a ten-month high, brokers said.
"The latest inflation figures definitely contributed to the market's weakness today and this is likely to maintain the pressure on (short-term interest) rates," a broker told Reuters.
The state Central Statistical Office says the consumer price index rose 2.5 percentage points to 22.4 percent from March's 19.9 percent.
Brokers and analysts say firming money market interest rates have destracted institutional buyers, the market's largest players, un-nerving individual investors who have sold heavily.

On Wednesday the index closed at 10,161.60, weighed down by losses in tobacco merchants Rothmans which tumbled 8.2 percent or 400 cents to 4,500, bankers Barclays down 100 or 3.3 percent to 2,900 cents and tobacco merchants BAT also down 100 to 1,500 cents.
Transporters Clan, clothing chain Edgars, multi-industrial group Delta DLTA.ZI, and finance house udc were all down 10 cents to 200, 715, 1,690 and 290 respectively.
But there were gains for newly listed National Merchant Bank up 50 cents, timber producers Border also plus 50 and drug manufacturers CAPS to 3,450, 1,650 and 1,800 respectively.
Mining shares were for a change firmer, up 13.10 points or 1.3 percent, lifted by an 11 percent or 1,000 cent surge in Ashanti to 10,000 and Bindura which rose 25 to 825 cents.
Seldom traded Mhangura, Rio Tinto and Wankie were all unchanged and the index vaulted back above the one thousand mark to 1000,11.
